### `fold_skills.py`

The owner's answers on the rest of the Skills, SK-1 and SK-2, folded into v2, the memory plan, the fates record, the gap register, the comparison record's [skills] and the session log.

````python
"""Fold the owner's answers on the rest of the Skills, SK-1 and SK-2: `/build` retires beside `/session-kickoff` and
`/unattended`, and the five question Skills stay as generated thin entries, every gov-rendered Skill named `gov-<name>`.
Edits v2 (the level-4 row, dWellOiledMachine's driver clause, two dConvergedCharter clauses and a third, `[open]` and a
revision note), the memory plan's Skills pocket, the fates record (the rendered-Skills row, a `/build` row, the counts),
the gap register (`gap-found-28` and the tally), the comparison record's `[skills]` and the session log's event.

Usage: python -X utf8 fold_skills.py <scratch-dir>   (from the worktree root)
"""
import pathlib
import re
import subprocess
import sys

S = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1])
sys.path.insert(0, str(S / "expansions"))
from fold_lib import Record  # noqa: E402

B = "memory/builds/dClosedLoop/build/"
COMPARED = "build/2026-10-18-build-PLAY-dClosedLoop-1-shape-reviews-compared.md"
F = "`" * 3
V = Record(B + "2026-10-14-build-PLAY-dClosedLoop-1-architecture-v2.md")
P = Record(B + "2026-10-18-build-PLAY-dClosedLoop-1-memory-plan.md")
T = Record(B + "2026-10-18-build-PLAY-dClosedLoop-1-fates.md")
G = Record(B + "2026-10-14-build-PLAY-dClosedLoop-1-gap-register.md")
C = Record(B + "2026-10-18-build-PLAY-dClosedLoop-1-shape-reviews-compared.md")
L = Record(B + "2026-10-14-build-PLAY-dClosedLoop-1-session-log.md")

said = {}
for ln in (S / "away" / "answers-skills.txt").read_text(encoding="utf-8").replace("\r\n", "\n").split("\n"):
    m = re.match(r"^(question|SK-\d) = (.+)$", ln)
    if m:
        said[m.group(1)] = m.group(2)
if sorted(said) != ["SK-1", "SK-2", "question"]:
    sys.exit(f"answers-skills.txt holds {sorted(said)}")

ROW = re.compile(r"^\| (d[A-Z]\w+) \| ([^|]+) \| ([^|]+) \| (.+) \| ([^|]+) \|$")


def chain_row(build):
    chain = V.text.split("\n## [chain]", 1)[1].split("\n## ", 1)[0]
    hits = [ln for ln in chain.split("\n") if ln.startswith(f"| {build} |")]
    if len(hits) != 1:
        sys.exit(f"[chain]: {len(hits)} rows for {build}")
    m = ROW.match(hits[0])
    return hits[0], m.group(2), m.group(3), m.group(4).split("; "), [g.strip() for g in m.group(5).split(",")]


def put(old, build, stage, parents, clauses, gaps):
    for c in clauses:
        if "; " in c or "|" in c:
            sys.exit(f"{build}: a clause holds '; ' or a pipe: {c[:80]}")
    V.sub(old, f"| {build} | {stage} | {parents} | {'; '.join(clauses)} | {', '.join(gaps)} |", f"chain {build}")


def at(clauses, opens):
    hits = [i for i, c in enumerate(clauses) if c.startswith(opens)]
    if len(hits) != 1:
        sys.exit(f"clause {opens!r}: {len(hits)} clauses open so")
    return hits[0]


# --- v2.
V.sub("| 4 | kit runbooks, Skills and path-scoped rules; a Skill is a thin entry: its trigger contract, the CLI command it "
      "shortcuts and the tags it enters, with no procedure of its own |",
      "| 4 | kit runbooks, Skills and path-scoped rules; a Skill is a thin entry: its trigger contract, the CLI command it "
      "shortcuts and the tags it enters, with no procedure of its own, generated from that command's drive row and, when "
      "gov renders it, named `gov-<name>` (SK-2) |", "level 4")
old, stage, parents, cl, gaps = chain_row("dWellOiledMachine")
i = at(cl, "the supervisor the only driver in every mode")
if not cl[i].endswith("each role act it hosts act-bound with that act's epoch (night pass, point 1)"):
    sys.exit("dWellOiledMachine's driver clause changed")
cl[i] = cl[i][:-len(" (night pass, point 1)")] + (", and `/build` reduced in the same unit to a client of `run`, which "
                                                  "dConvergedCharter retires (night pass, point 1, SK-1)")
put(old, "dWellOiledMachine", stage, parents, cl, gaps)
old, stage, parents, cl, gaps = chain_row("dConvergedCharter")
i = at(cl, "Skills converged to level-4 thin entries")
if cl[i] != "Skills converged to level-4 thin entries, each described \"Use when …, runs …\"":
    sys.exit("dConvergedCharter's Skills clause changed")
cl[i] = ("Skills converged to level-4 thin entries, each generated from the drive row of the command it runs and never "
         "hand-written, described \"Use when …, runs …\", installed with that command, and named `gov-<name>` where gov "
         "renders it: `/gov-recall` over `gov why` and `record find` and `/gov-runlog` over `gov trace`, both core, and "
         "`/gov-lexicon`, `/gov-drift-audit` and `/gov-cleanup` with their kits, each rename shipped as an upgrade step "
         "with the old name forwarded for `install.deprecation-window` releases, and the Skill kind's conformance gate "
         "refusing a gov-rendered Skill without the prefix, seen red on a planted one (SK-2)")
i = at(cl, "the `/session-kickoff` Skill retired")
cl.insert(i + 1, "the `/build` Skill retired once dWellOiledMachine's supervisor drives attended builds: a `[[retired]]` "
                 "row with its readers inventoried by value, the charter's attended-build line, the roles kit's skill "
                 "template, its install row and probe, and its harness wiring, and the kickoff card's hand-off to it, the "
                 "client dWellOiledMachine left kept for `install.deprecation-window` releases, then removed (SK-1)")
put(old, "dConvergedCharter", stage, parents, cl, gaps + ["gap-found-28"])
V.sub("  a page.\n\n## [owed]",
      "  a page.\n\n"
      f"Open, 2026-10-19, from the owner's answers on the rest of the Skills (`{COMPARED}` `[skills]`):\n"
      "- SK-2's `/gov-lexicon` and `/gov-drift-audit` follow the owner's pattern, beside the owner's own `/gov-recall`,\n"
      "  `/gov-runlog` and `/gov-cleanup`.\n\n## [owed]", "open")
V.sub("corpus declare their legacy populations, every rename and retirement inventories its readers by value, and every\n"
      "set-valued key says whether it may be empty.\n\n",
      "corpus declare their legacy populations, every rename and retirement inventories its readers by value, and every\n"
      "set-valued key says whether it may be empty.\n\n"
      f"Revised: 2026-10-19, the owner's answers on the rest of the Skills (`{COMPARED}` `[skills]`): `/build` retires\n"
      "beside `/session-kickoff` and `/unattended`, a client of `run` from dWellOiledMachine until dConvergedCharter\n"
      "removes it (SK-1); and the five question Skills stay as thin entries generated from their commands' drive rows,\n"
      "every gov-rendered Skill named `gov-<name>` (SK-2).\n\n", "revision note")

# --- The memory plan.
P.sub("| Skills and path rules | instruction | `.claude/skills/`, `.claude/rules/` | 0 tagged | node: thin entries at level 4 |",
      "| Skills and path rules | instruction | `.claude/skills/`, `.claude/rules/` | 0 tagged | node: thin entries at level "
      "4, each generated from its command's drive row, gov's named `gov-<name>` (SK-2) |", "pocket Skills")

# --- The fates record.
T.sub("| skills | rendered Skills, six of seven, `/unattended` apart | entries | RESHAPED | thin level-4 entries; `/build` "
      "becomes a client of `next` and `run` (dConvergedCharter, with dWellOiledMachine for the client) | layer-instruction "
      "`[recommendations]`; layer-runtime `[decide]` |",
      "| skills | rendered Skills, five of seven, `/unattended` and `/build` apart | entries | RESHAPED | thin level-4 "
      "entries generated from their commands' drive rows and renamed `gov-<name>`: `/gov-recall` and `/gov-runlog` core, "
      "`/gov-lexicon`, `/gov-drift-audit` and `/gov-cleanup` with their kits (dConvergedCharter) | layer-instruction "
      "`[recommendations]`; layer-runtime `[decide]`; the owner, SK-2, 2026-10-19 |", "row rendered Skills")
anchor = [ln for ln in T.text.split("\n") if ln.startswith("| roles | `.claude/roles.json` |")]
if len(anchor) != 1:
    sys.exit("the roles.json row moved")
T.sub(anchor[0] + "\n", anchor[0] + "\n"
      "| roles | the `/build` Skill | drives an attended build through the harness pipeline | RETIRED | a client of `run` "
      "once the supervisor drives attended builds (dWellOiledMachine), removed after the deprecation window "
      "(dConvergedCharter) | the owner, SK-1, 2026-10-19 |\n", "row build")
table = T.text.split("\n## [table]", 1)[1].split("\n## ", 1)[0]
fates = [ln.split(" | ")[3] for ln in table.split("\n") if ln.startswith("| ") and not ln.startswith("| Kit |")
         and not ln.startswith("|---")]
n = {f: fates.count(f) for f in ("STAYS", "RESHAPED", "MERGED", "RETIRED")}
if sum(n.values()) != len(fates):
    sys.exit(f"a fate outside the closed set: {sorted(set(fates))}")
m = re.search(r"Counts: (\d+) stay,\n(\d+) reshaped, (\d+) merged and (\d+) retired, over (\d+) rows\.", T.text)
if not m:
    sys.exit("the fates counts sentence moved")
T.sub(m.group(0), f"Counts: {n['STAYS']} stay,\n{n['RESHAPED']} reshaped, {n['MERGED']} merged and {n['RETIRED']} "
      f"retired, over {len(fates)} rows.", "counts")

# --- The gap register.
row27 = [ln for ln in G.text.split("\n") if ln.startswith("| gap-found-27 |")]
if len(row27) != 1:
    sys.exit("gap-found-27 moved")
G.sub(row27[0] + "\n", row27[0] + "\n"
      "| gap-found-28 | Foundation | LOW | gov's rendered Skills carry bare names, `/build`, `/cleanup`, `/lexicon`, "
      "`/runlog` and the rest, which nothing marks as gov's beside a repository's or a user's own Skills. | the owner, "
      "SK-2, 2026-10-19 | — |\n", "gap-found-28")

# --- The comparison record.
C.text = C.text.rstrip("\n") + f"""

## [skills] The rest of the Skills, 2026-10-19

After SA-9, the owner asked:

> {said['question']}

The records answered it. Of today's nine Skills, three were already set to retire: `/session-kickoff` (SA-9),
`/unattended` (NP-4) and `deploy-governance` (`gap-tool-05`). `/build`, which drives an attended build, would be a
second door beside a placed request, since the supervisor drives every build and `attend` makes one attended. The five
question Skills do not enter the flow: their procedures dissolve into commands, which leaves each a trigger line and a
command, a slash shortcut for the owner and a trigger the model matches, at the cost of repeating the charter's drive
line in every session. Two forks went to the owner, each with its recommendation first:

| Fork | Question | The owner's answer |
|---|---|---|
| SK-1 | retire `/build` once the supervisor drives attended builds, as with `/session-kickoff`? | "{said['SK-1']}" |
| SK-2 | keep the five question Skills as generated one-line shortcuts? | "{said['SK-2']}" |

How the answers were read:
- **SK-1:** `/build` becomes a client of `run` in the unit where dWellOiledMachine's supervisor becomes the only driver,
  and dConvergedCharter retires it, with its readers inventoried by value and the client kept for the deprecation
  window.
- **SK-2:** the five stay as thin entries, each generated from its command's drive row and never hand-written, and
  every gov-rendered Skill is named `gov-<name>`: `/gov-recall` and `/gov-runlog`, the owner's names, core shortcuts
  over `gov why`, `record find` and `gov trace`; `/gov-cleanup`, the owner's name; and `/gov-lexicon` and
  `/gov-drift-audit`, read from the owner's "etc.", which v2's `[open]` keeps to confirm. Each rename ships as an upgrade
  step with its old name forwarded for the window, and the Skill kind's conformance gate refuses a gov-rendered Skill
  without the prefix. `gap-found-28` records today's bare names.

Folded: v2's level-4 row, dWellOiledMachine's driver clause, dConvergedCharter's Skills clause and a new `/build`
clause, `[open]` and a revision note; the memory plan's Skills pocket; the fates record's rendered-Skills row and a
`/build` row; and `gap-found-28`, with the register's tally re-measured.
"""
C.done += 1

L.insert_before("\n## Instruments\n", f"""
- 2026-10-19, session 1799cb98: the owner asked whether the rest of the Skills still serve a purpose. The records
  answered it, and two forks followed (`{COMPARED}` `[skills]`): `/build` retires beside `/session-kickoff` and
  `/unattended` (SK-1), and the five question Skills stay as generated thin entries, every gov-rendered Skill named
  `gov-<name>` (SK-2).
""", "event")

for rec in (V, P, T, G, C, L):
    rec.save()

tally = subprocess.run(["awk", "-F|", "-f", str(S / "away" / "tally.awk"), str(G.path)], capture_output=True, text=True,
                       check=True).stdout.replace("\r\n", "\n").strip("\n").split("\n")
counts = [ln.rstrip() for ln in tally]
total = sum(int(kv.split("=")[1]) for kv in counts[0].split())
G.text = G.text.rstrip("\n") + f"""

Re-measured after the owner's SK-2 added `gap-found-28` (`{COMPARED}` `[skills]`), same instrument, over {total} keys:

{F}text
{counts[0]}
{counts[1]}
{F}
"""
G.done += 1
G.save()
print(f"register: {total} gaps; fates: {n}, {len(fates)} rows")

### `rewrap_skills.py`

Rewraps the two [skills] paragraphs the confirmation lengthened, at 120 columns; a doubled space it left after the list dash was fixed by hand.

````python
"""Rewrap the two [skills] paragraphs the name confirmation lengthened, at the records' 120 columns."""
import pathlib
import sys

p = pathlib.Path("memory/builds/dClosedLoop/build/2026-10-18-build-PLAY-dClosedLoop-1-shape-reviews-compared.md")
t = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")


def wrap(text, first, rest):
    out, cur = [], first
    for w in text.split(" "):
        cand = (cur + " " + w) if cur.strip() else cur + w
        if len(cand) > 120 and cur.strip():
            out.append(cur)
            cur = rest + w
        else:
            cur = cand
    out.append(cur)
    return "\n".join(out)


start = t.index("- **SK-2:** the five stay as thin entries")
end = t.index("`gap-found-28` records today's bare names.\n", start) + len("`gap-found-28` records today's bare names.")
block = " ".join(ln.strip() for ln in t[start:end].split("\n"))
t = t[:start] + wrap(block[len("- "):], "- ", "  ") + t[end:]
start = t.index("The owner confirmed the names on 2026-10-19:")
end = t.index("rendered-Skills row.\n", start) + len("rendered-Skills row.")
block = " ".join(ln.strip() for ln in t[start:end].split("\n"))
t = t[:start] + wrap(block, "", "") + t[end:]
long = [ln for ln in t[t.index("## [skills]"):].split("\n") if len(ln) > 120 and not ln.startswith(("|", ">"))]
if long:   # table rows and the quoted question cannot wrap; prose can
    sys.exit(f"a [skills] prose line still runs past 120 columns: {long[0][:80]}")
p.write_text(t, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
print("rewrapped")
````

### `save_return.py`

night/save_return.py with the record's date as an argument: saves each researcher's return verbatim as a research record.

````python
"""Save one agent's final return, verbatim, as a research record in the build folder: night/save_return.py with the
record's date as an argument, since that script writes 2026-10-18 into every name it makes.

Usage: python -X utf8 save_return.py <date> <transcript.jsonl> <record-name> <title> <dispatch> <prompt-file> <use>
  date         the record's date, e.g. 2026-10-19
  record-name  e.g. research-adopter-today, saved as build/<date>-build-PLAY-dClosedLoop-1-<record-name>.md
  title        the record's H1, after "Research: "
  dispatch     the session log's dispatch number
  prompt-file  the handoff's file name under prompts/
  use          where the return is used, a record name under build/, dated the same day

Reads the transcript's last assistant message, joins its text blocks, demotes any H1 to bold, and writes the record.
Prints the record's path, its size and the return's first line only. Refuses to overwrite.
"""
import json
import pathlib
import re
import sys

date, src, name, title, dispatch, prompt, use = sys.argv[1:8]
if not re.fullmatch(r"\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}", date):
    sys.exit("the date reads YYYY-MM-DD")
last = None
with open(src, encoding="utf-8") as f:
    for line in f:
        try:
            ev = json.loads(line)
        except ValueError:
            continue
        msg = ev.get("message") if isinstance(ev, dict) else None
        if ev.get("type") == "assistant" and isinstance(msg, dict):
            texts = [b.get("text", "") for b in msg.get("content", []) if isinstance(b, dict) and b.get("type") == "text"]
            if any(t.strip() for t in texts):
                last = "\n".join(t for t in texts if t.strip())
if not last:
    sys.exit("no assistant text in " + src)
body = re.sub(r"^# (.+)$", r"**\1**", last.replace("\r\n", "\n").strip("\n"), flags=re.M)
out = pathlib.Path("memory/builds/dClosedLoop/build/%s-build-PLAY-dClosedLoop-1-%s.md" % (date, name))
if out.exists():
    sys.exit("%s exists" % out)
head = ("# Research: %s\n\n**Serves:** research PLAY-dClosedLoop-1\n\n"
        "This is dispatch %s's return, verbatim, except that a title line would be demoted to keep one H1 per record. "
        "Its question is in `prompts/%s`, and its use is in `build/%s-build-PLAY-dClosedLoop-1-%s.md`.\n\n---\n\n"
        % (title, dispatch, prompt, date, use))
out.write_text(head + body + "\n", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
print("%s · %d bytes · first line: %s" % (out, out.stat().st_size, body.split("\n", 1)[0][:100]))
````

### `dispatch_prompt.py`

Builds each researcher's dispatch prompt from its rendered handoff: the marker line, then the handoff from its Task section on.

````python
"""Build a dispatch prompt from a rendered handoff: its marker line, then the handoff from `## Task` to its end."""
import pathlib
import re
import sys

text = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]).read_text(encoding="utf-8").replace("\r\n", "\n")
marker = [ln for ln in text.split("\n") if re.fullmatch(r"<!-- gov:handoff .* -->", ln)]
if len(marker) != 1 or "\n## Task\n" not in text:
    sys.exit("no single marker line, or no Task section")
out = marker[0] + "\n\n" + "## Task\n" + text.split("\n## Task\n", 1)[1]
pathlib.Path(sys.argv[2]).write_text(out, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
print(sys.argv[2], len(out))
````

### `peek_dispatch.py`

Reads an earlier Agent dispatch's shape from the session transcript, to match it.

````python
"""Print the shape of one earlier Agent dispatch: the first lines and the length of its prompt."""
import json
import sys

needle = sys.argv[2]
with open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    for line in fh:
        if '"Agent"' not in line or needle not in line:
            continue
        rec = json.loads(line)
        for b in rec.get("message", {}).get("content", []) or []:
            if isinstance(b, dict) and b.get("type") == "tool_use" and b.get("name") == "Agent":
                p = b["input"].get("prompt", "")
                if needle in p:
                    print({k: v for k, v in b["input"].items() if k != "prompt"})
                    print(len(p), "chars; first lines:")
                    print("\n".join(p.split("\n")[:8]))
                    print("... last line:", p.rstrip().split("\n")[-1][:160])
                    sys.exit(0)
print("not found")
````

### `fold_adopt.py`

The owner's answers to IA-1 to IA-6 folded into v2, the memory plan, the gap register, the fates record, the design record and the session log.

````python
"""Fold the owner's answers to IA-1 to IA-6, the adopter-instructions forks, into v2 (P8, two catalogue keys and their
preset rows, six chain rows, [owed] and a revision note), the memory plan (two pockets and the unit site), the gap
register (five gaps and the tally), the fates record (a retired seed, the house files and the counts), the design
record's [answers] and [folded], and the session log's event.

Usage: python -X utf8 fold_adopt.py <scratch-dir>   (from the worktree root)
"""
import pathlib
import re
import subprocess
import sys

S = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1])
sys.path.insert(0, str(S / "expansions"))
from fold_lib import Record  # noqa: E402

B = "memory/builds/dClosedLoop/build/"
REC = "build/2026-10-19-build-PLAY-dClosedLoop-1-adopter-instructions.md"
F = "`" * 3
V = Record(B + "2026-10-14-build-PLAY-dClosedLoop-1-architecture-v2.md")
P = Record(B + "2026-10-18-build-PLAY-dClosedLoop-1-memory-plan.md")
G = Record(B + "2026-10-14-build-PLAY-dClosedLoop-1-gap-register.md")
T = Record(B + "2026-10-18-build-PLAY-dClosedLoop-1-fates.md")
A = Record(B + "2026-10-19-build-PLAY-dClosedLoop-1-adopter-instructions.md")
L = Record(B + "2026-10-14-build-PLAY-dClosedLoop-1-session-log.md")

said = {}
for ln in (S / "adopt" / "answers-adopt.txt").read_text(encoding="utf-8").replace("\r\n", "\n").split("\n"):
    m = re.match(r"^(IA-\d) = (.+)$", ln)
    if m:
        said[m.group(1)] = m.group(2)
if sorted(said) != [f"IA-{i}" for i in range(1, 7)]:
    sys.exit(f"answers-adopt.txt holds {sorted(said)}")

ROW = re.compile(r"^\| (d[A-Z]\w+) \| ([^|]+) \| ([^|]+) \| (.+) \| ([^|]+) \|$")


def chain_row(build):
    chain = V.text.split("\n## [chain]", 1)[1].split("\n## ", 1)[0]
    hits = [ln for ln in chain.split("\n") if ln.startswith(f"| {build} |")]
    if len(hits) != 1:
        sys.exit(f"[chain]: {len(hits)} rows for {build}")
    m = ROW.match(hits[0])
    return hits[0], m.group(2), m.group(3), m.group(4).split("; "), [g.strip() for g in m.group(5).split(",")]


def put(old, build, stage, parents, clauses, gaps):
    for c in clauses:
        if "; " in c or "|" in c:
            sys.exit(f"{build}: a clause holds '; ' or a pipe: {c[:80]}")
    V.sub(old, f"| {build} | {stage} | {parents} | {'; '.join(clauses)} | {', '.join(gaps)} |", f"chain {build}")


def at(clauses, opens):
    hits = [i for i, c in enumerate(clauses) if c.startswith(opens)]
    if len(hits) != 1:
        sys.exit(f"clause {opens!r}: {len(hits)} clauses open so")
    return hits[0]


def edit(clauses, opens, old, new):
    i = at(clauses, opens)
    if clauses[i].count(old) != 1:
        sys.exit(f"clause {opens!r}: {old!r} is not in it once")
    clauses[i] = clauses[i].replace(old, new)


# --- v2: P8, the catalogue, the presets.
V.sub("- **P8 Every adopter is an adopter, gov included.** The charter is the shared foundation; each\n"
      "  repository's own rules render from its own overlay as a separate project block (walk CV1).\n",
      "- **P8 Every adopter is an adopter, gov included.** The charter is the shared foundation; each\n"
      "  repository's own rules render from its own overlay as a separate project block (walk CV1). A repository changes\n"
      "  gov's units only through its own units' typed edges, pinned to the gov text they were written against, so an\n"
      "  update never overwrites or silently drops a repository's change (IA-1 to IA-6).\n", "P8")
proof_row = [ln for ln in V.text.split("\n") if ln.startswith("| `instructions.proof` |")]
if len(proof_row) != 1:
    sys.exit("no single instructions.proof row")
V.sub(proof_row[0] + "\n", proof_row[0] + "\n"
      "| `instructions.exclude` | none, or a set of gov unit tags, a fixed unit and one another active unit requires "
      "refused | none | the adopter-instructions pass: the gov units a repository drops, as `charter.practices` does "
      "for practices; the owner's IA-2; never set by a preset | dOrderedCharter |\n"
      "| `instructions.stale` | order, refuse, warn | order | the adopter-instructions pass: what an update does when a "
      "semantic change to a gov unit leaves a repository's `amends` or `supersedes` edge behind it, an editorial change "
      "never flagging; the owner's IA-3 | dOrderedCharter |\n", "catalogue rows")
V.sub("  `instructions.edit`, `instructions.proof`, `policy.on-missing-expansion`, `release.environments`,\n",
      "  `instructions.edit`, `instructions.proof`, `instructions.exclude`, `policy.on-missing-expansion`,\n"
      "  `release.environments`,\n", "presets never touch")
checks_preset = [ln for ln in V.text.split("\n") if ln.startswith("| `instructions.checks` | warn |")]
if len(checks_preset) != 1:
    sys.exit("no single instructions.checks preset row")
V.sub(checks_preset[0] + "\n", checks_preset[0] + "\n| `instructions.stale` | warn | order | refuse | order |\n",
      "preset row")

# --- v2's chain.
old, stage, parents, cl, gaps = chain_row("dGroundRules")
edit(cl, "the minimal guard", "its JSON mirror, the instruction manifest and",
     "its JSON mirror, the instruction manifest, which is the repository's overlay `.governance/instructions.toml`, and")
put(old, "dGroundRules", stage, parents, cl, gaps)

old, stage, parents, cl, gaps = chain_row("dSafePassage")
edit(cl, "the step gate", "record-kind schemas and policy keys among them, joining when its owning build lands it,",
     "record-kind schemas, policy keys and gov's instruction-unit tags among them, joining when its owning build lands "
     "it, a unit tag vanishing only with a change record naming its successor,")
edit(cl, "withdrawn hook fragments unwired", "not graded as a fork by arm 3c (P38, SA-2)",
     "not graded as a fork by arm 3c, and an edited rendered file named at update and held with an order, never "
     "reported as `re-rendered` (P38, SA-2, IA-2)")
put(old, "dSafePassage", stage, parents, cl, gaps)

old, stage, parents, cl, gaps = chain_row("dOrderedCharter")
edit(cl, "the instruction-unit registry", "budget class, source, owning kit)",
     "budget class, source, owner, a kit or the repository, and class, fixed or open)")
edit(cl, "the namespaced tag system", "principle, kind, record, kit), of which it registers reader, level, layer, "
     "practice, principle, kind and kit,",
     "principle, kind, record, kit, repo), of which it registers reader, level, layer, practice, principle, kind, kit "
     "and repo, the repository's own,")
cl += [
    "the repository's instruction overlay: `.governance/instructions.toml`, one guarded home in each kit manifest's "
    "row grammar, its rows owned by the repository and tagged in the `repo.` namespace, absorbing `deploy.toml`'s "
    "adopter rules as level-0 units, its units added by level, `select` and `when`, and gov's units changed only "
    "through a repository unit's `amends`, rendered after gov's unit, or `supersedes`, rendered in its place, each "
    "target pinned as `<tag>@<hash>`, a whitespace-normalised hash of gov's text, or excluded through "
    "`instructions.exclude`, every gov unit declaring its class, a fixed one (the core principles, the floor's "
    "invariants and every unit a gov tool parses) refusing all three, and a repository's own keys under `repo.` read "
    "only by its units, each operation seen on a planted overlay and each refusal red (IA-1, IA-2, IA-4)",
    "pins and drift: each gov change record marked `editorial` or `semantic`, a pin behind editorial changes alone "
    "standing, a semantic change rendering gov's new text and the repository's change and filing an order as "
    "`instructions.stale` says, a rename re-pointing the edge to the change record's successor, a split or a "
    "retirement orphaning it, an orphaned amendment held out of the render and an orphaned replacement rendered on its "
    "own, each with an order, and the update listing every new gov unit at a level and `select` the repository has "
    "units in, each case seen on a planted release (IA-3)",
    "composition and its report: the project block from the repository's level-0 units and its level-3 to level-5 "
    "units in a marked part of their documents, its units counted against each budget and an overflow refused "
    "naming the largest contributors by owner, never truncated, every harness rendering the same units so no alias is "
    "a copy, the seeded charter template retired, a delta report at every update naming each gov unit's state, and the "
    "shipped foundation set holding only what every adopter needs, by a census of today's practices that the owner "
    "rules one by one, the gov-only ones moving to gov's own overlay (P8, IA-6)",
]
put(old, "dOrderedCharter", stage, parents, cl, gaps + ["gap-found-29", "gap-found-30", "gap-found-31"])

old, stage, parents, cl, gaps = chain_row("dBoundRoles")
cl.append("the roles kit's house files moved into the repository's overlay as level-5 units selecting their role, "
          "with their own upgrade step (IA-1, P38)")
put(old, "dBoundRoles", stage, parents, cl, gaps)

old, stage, parents, cl, gaps = chain_row("dLinkedLibrary")
cl.append("`adopt.instructions`: at install an adopter's own instruction files rendered verbatim as a legacy block "
          "after the project block, on a shrink-only list, every harness file wired at once and none overwritten, then "
          "each paragraph proposed as a repository unit, an amendment of a gov unit or a drop, for the owner to rule "
          "once (IA-5)")
put(old, "dLinkedLibrary", stage, parents, cl, gaps + ["gap-deploy-26"])

old, stage, parents, cl, gaps = chain_row("dShippedRelease")
edit(cl, "the install and update hooks", "run attended until no tree is left on shards (NP-22)",
     "run attended until no tree is left on shards (NP-22), and a fresh install of every kit in one pass, the kits' "
     "adopters ordered by their declared dependencies and seen on an empty repository")
put(old, "dShippedRelease", stage, parents, cl, gaps + ["gap-deploy-27"])

V.sub("  - the code record's cold derivation re-timed at dTotalRecall's first unit:",
      f"  - the pin's noise, re-measured at dOrderedCharter's first unit over units of one line against gov's history\n"
      f"    (`{REC}` `[owed]`);\n"
      "  - the code record's cold derivation re-timed at dTotalRecall's first unit:", "owed")
V.sub("the names confirmed with `/gov-drift` in place of\n`/gov-drift-audit`.\n\n",
      "the names confirmed with `/gov-drift` in place of\n`/gov-drift-audit`.\n\n"
      f"Revised: 2026-10-19, the owner's answers to the adopter-instructions forks (`{REC}` `[answers]`): a repository's\n"
      "own instructions live in one guarded overlay, `.governance/instructions.toml`, tagged `repo.` (IA-1); it changes\n"
      "gov's units only by `amends` and `supersedes` edges pinned to gov's text, or excludes them by\n"
      "`instructions.exclude` (IA-2); a semantic change to an amended unit renders both and files an order, an\n"
      "editorial one never flags (IA-3); the core principles, the floor and what gov's tools parse stay fixed (IA-4);\n"
      "an adopter's own instruction files become a legacy block at install, then proposals (IA-5); and gov's own rules\n"
      "move to gov's overlay by a census the owner rules on (IA-6). dOrderedCharter gains three units, dBoundRoles and\n"
      "dLinkedLibrary one each, and P8 says how a repository changes gov's units.\n\n", "revision note")

# --- The memory plan.
dep = [ln for ln in P.text.split("\n") if ln.startswith("| deploy overlay |")]
if len(dep) != 1:
    sys.exit("no single deploy overlay pocket")
P.sub(dep[0] + "\n",
      "| deploy overlay | instruction | `.governance/deploy.toml`, committed | the repository's install answers and kit "
      "selection, and today its adopter rules, rendered into the charter | node: units at level 0, written only through "
      "`instructions.edit`, under dGroundRules' minimal guard (SA-12), its adopter rules moving into the instruction "
      "overlay (IA-1) | tag | dOrderedCharter |\n"
      "| instruction overlay | instruction | `.governance/instructions.toml`, committed | designed: the repository's own "
      "units, today spread across `deploy.toml`'s adopter rules and the roles' house files | node: the repository's "
      "units, tagged `repo.`, changing gov's only by `amends` and `supersedes` edges pinned to gov's text (IA-1, IA-2) "
      "| tag | dOrderedCharter |\n", "pockets")
P.sub("| an instruction unit | its row's `select`, `required-by` and `enforced-by` fields, as today, and `edges` in the "
      "same grammar |",
      "| an instruction unit | its row's `select`, `required-by` and `enforced-by` fields, as today, and `edges` in the "
      "same grammar, an `amends` or `supersedes` target pinned as `<tag>@<hash>` |", "sites")

# --- The gap register.
GAPS = [
    ("gap-found-28", "| gap-found-29 | Foundation | HIGH | No seam changes or removes a gov instruction and keeps the "
     "change: the overlay slot and the roles' house files only add, an edit to a rendered instruction is overwritten "
     "at update and named only `re-rendered`, a tagged edit is lost the same way, and an edit to gov's own source holds "
     "the whole kit back on a conflict. | `research-adopter-today.md` sections 2 and 5 | — |\n"
     "| gap-found-30 | Foundation | MED | A seeded charter template freezes at its install vintage, edited or not, "
     "graded `reseed-available`. | `research-adopter-today.md` section 2 | — |\n"
     "| gap-found-31 | Foundation | MED | Gov's own rules ship in the set every adopter receives: their move to gov's "
     "own overlay, decided by the walk, was dropped at `aa0d778b1`. | `research-adopter-design.md`, contradiction 4 | "
     "— |\n"),
    ("gap-deploy-25", "| gap-deploy-26 | Deploy | MED | An adopter's own `CLAUDE.md`, `GEMINI.md` and Copilot "
     "instructions stay unwired at install until `--force` overwrites them, and a copy-mode alias goes stale at every "
     "charter change with no check at update. | `research-adopter-today.md` sections 2 and 3 | — |\n"
     "| gap-deploy-27 | Deploy | MED | A fresh install of every kit needs manual steps: on an empty repository the "
     "kickoff seed creates `memory/` before the memory tree's adopter, which then refuses, and the agent-instructions "
     "adopter runs before the charter exists. | `research-adopter-today.md`, its fixture notes | — |\n"),
]
for after, rows in GAPS:
    hit = [ln for ln in G.text.split("\n") if ln.startswith(f"| {after} |")]
    if len(hit) != 1:
        sys.exit(f"no single row {after}")
    G.sub(hit[0] + "\n", hit[0] + "\n" + rows, f"after {after}")

# --- The fates record.
T.sub("| roles | `agents/*`, `house/*.md` | role definitions | RESHAPED | twelve core roles with structured fields and "

      "IA-1) |", "row roles")
pb = [ln for ln in T.text.split("\n") if ln.startswith("| playbook | `adopt-playbook --check` |")]
if len(pb) != 1:
    sys.exit("no single adopt-playbook row")
T.sub(pb[0] + "\n", pb[0] + "\n"
      "| playbook | the seeded charter template | an adopter's copy of the template, frozen at its install vintage | "
      "RETIRED | units the one renderer composes, the repository's changes in its own overlay (dOrderedCharter) | the "
      "owner, IA-1, 2026-10-19 |\n", "row seed")
table = T.text.split("\n## [table]", 1)[1].split("\n## ", 1)[0]
fates = [ln.split(" | ")[3] for ln in table.split("\n") if ln.startswith("| ") and not ln.startswith("| Kit |")
         and not ln.startswith("|---")]
n = {f: fates.count(f) for f in ("STAYS", "RESHAPED", "MERGED", "RETIRED")}
if sum(n.values()) != len(fates):

      f"retired, over {len(fates)} rows.", "counts")

# --- The design record's answers.
rows = "\n".join(f"| IA-{i} | \"{said[f'IA-{i}']}\" |" for i in range(1, 7))

  `instructions.stale`, the first among the keys presets never touch and the second with a preset row; dGroundRules'
  minimal guard names the overlay; dSafePassage's step gate takes gov's unit tags and its update holds an edited
  render; dOrderedCharter's registry gains a unit's owner and class and the `repo` namespace, and three units: the
  overlay and its operations, pins and drift, and composition with the census of gov-only rules; dBoundRoles moves the
  house files into the overlay; dLinkedLibrary gains `adopt.instructions`; dShippedRelease installs every kit in one
  pass; `[owed]` keeps the pin's noise to re-measure; and a revision note.
- **The memory plan:** the deploy overlay's adopter rules move to a new instruction-overlay pocket, and the unit site
  carries the pinned target.
- **The gap register:** `gap-found-29`, `gap-found-30`, `gap-found-31`, `gap-deploy-26` and `gap-deploy-27`.
- **The fates record:** the seeded charter template retires, and the house files become overlay units.
"""
A.done += 2

L.insert_before("\n## Instruments\n", f"""
- 2026-10-19, session 1799cb98: the owner answered the adopter-instructions forks, IA-1 to IA-6, each with its
  recommendation (`{REC}` `[answers]`), and the answers are folded into v2, the memory plan, the gap register and the
  fates record.
""", "event")

for rec in (V, P, G, T, A, L):
    rec.save()

tally = subprocess.run(["awk", "-F|", "-f", str(S / "away" / "tally.awk"), str(G.path)], capture_output=True, text=True,
                       check=True).stdout.replace("\r\n", "\n").strip("\n").split("\n")
counts = [ln.rstrip() for ln in tally]
total = sum(int(kv.split("=")[1]) for kv in counts[0].split())
G.text = G.text.rstrip("\n") + f"""

Re-measured after the adopter-instructions answers added `gap-found-29`, `gap-found-30`, `gap-found-31`,
`gap-deploy-26` and `gap-deploy-27` (`{REC}` `[folded]`), same instrument, over {total} keys:

{F}text
{counts[0]}
{counts[1]}
{F}
"""
G.done += 1
G.save()
print(f"register: {total} gaps; fates: {n}, {len(fates)} rows")
````

### `build_args_folds.py`

The args of the last three folds' closing review, runs A and B, differing only in the run label, the report path and the scratch path.

````python
"""Build the args of the closing review of the last three folds, run twice at the owner's word ("Run the reviews of the
same shape (medium effort, twice) for the last three folds", 2026-10-19): two independent light Tier-2 diff reviews of
dd1ebb01b..320c79646, every role at medium, the shape of the answers fold's closing review
(`away/build_args_answers.py`). The two runs differ only in the run label, the report path and the scratch path.

Usage: python -X utf8 build_args_folds.py <scratch-dir> <base> <head>   (from the worktree root)
Writes <scratch-dir>/adopt/args-folds-a.json and args-folds-b.json, and a compact copy of each.
"""
import json
import pathlib
import subprocess
import sys

S, BASE, HEAD = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]), sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
B = "memory/builds/dClosedLoop/build/"
R = "memory/builds/dClosedLoop/reviews/2026-10-19-review-PLAY-dClosedLoop-1-folds-closing-{}.md"
base = json.loads((S / "away" / "args-answers-a.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
full = lambda r: subprocess.run(["git", "rev-parse", r], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout.strip()
base["base"], base["head"] = full(BASE), full(HEAD)
base["intensity"], base["round"] = "light", 1
base["efforts"] = {"diffFinder": "medium", "skeptic": "medium", "synthesis": "medium"}
base["specs"] = base["specs"] + [
    B + "2026-10-18-build-PLAY-dClosedLoop-1-shape-reviews-compared.md",
    B + "2026-10-19-build-PLAY-dClosedLoop-1-adopter-instructions.md",
    B + "2026-10-19-build-PLAY-dClosedLoop-1-research-adopter-today.md",
    B + "2026-10-19-build-PLAY-dClosedLoop-1-research-adopter-design.md",
    B + "2026-10-19-build-PLAY-dClosedLoop-1-research-adopter-prior-art.md",
    B + "2026-10-19-build-PLAY-dClosedLoop-1-research-adopter-history.md",
    "memory/builds/dClosedLoop/reviews/2026-10-18-review-PLAY-dClosedLoop-1-shape-audit-a.md",
    "memory/builds/dClosedLoop/reviews/2026-10-18-review-PLAY-dClosedLoop-1-shape-audit-b.md",
]
if len(set(base["specs"])) != len(base["specs"]):
    sys.exit("a spec repeats")
for p in base["specs"]:
    if not pathlib.Path(p).exists():
        sys.exit(f"missing: {p}")
base["checklist"] = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "tools/memory-tree/gotchas.py", "--for-diff", f"{BASE}..{HEAD}"],
                                   capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8", check=True).stdout
base["byDesign"] = "\n".join([
    "- The build is design-only: no product code and no unit specs. Unit-level detail is absent by design and owed to "
    "the chain builds, and a row's planned units are prose, counted one per clause.",
    "- The owner's words are decisions where they direct, recorded verbatim: the answers to the shape audit's forks "
    "SA-1 to SA-12 (the shape comparison record's [answers]), to SK-1 and SK-2 with the confirmed names (its [skills]), "
    "and to IA-1 to IA-6 (the adopter-instructions record's [answers]). A finding may show a fold contradicting the "
    "owner's words, a record or the tree, not re-argue the owner's direction.",
    "- Two readings stay open for the owner in v2's [open]: SA-1's \"layer date\" read as \"a later date\", and SA-5's "
    "field named `usage`. A finding may show that one contradicts the owner's words or a record, not argue a "
    "preference.",
    "- Every earlier answer stands: SA-1 to SA-12, SK-1 and SK-2, IA-1 to IA-6, AP-1 to AP-35, NP-1 to NP-24, SP-1 and "
    "SP-2, WK-1 to WK-8, PM-1 to PM-12, RC-1 to RC-9, AF-1 to AF-3, FL1, CX-1 to CX-3, RT-1 to RT-4, and every round's "
    "before them.",
    "- Research returns are verbatim and dated, dispatches 118 to 121's among them, and their prompts are rendered "
    "handoffs: neither is under review, though a record that misstates its return is. The shape audit's two reports "
    "are reviews of their own subjects, not under review.",
    "- Dated records keep what held when they were written: revision notes, the session log's past entries, and the "
    "shape comparison record's [map], [summary] and [forks], which state the design at dd1ebb01b.",
    "- The instruments record holds the scripts as they ran; a script is reviewed only for whether it did what the "
    "records say it did.",
    "- Generated files (memory/LIVE.md, the build README's generated regions and memory/gotchas/INDEX.md) are "
    "rendered, not reviewed. The nineteen bug-class instances are reviewed for faithfulness to the defects they name.",
])
CONTEXT = (
    "The diff is " + base["head"][:9] + " over " + base["base"][:9] + ": three folds. "
    "(1) 23baa12de folds the whole-design shape audit: its 66 confirmed defects, each by the comparison record's "
    "[fold] (" + B + "2026-10-18-build-PLAY-dClosedLoop-1-shape-reviews-compared.md), and the owner's answers to its "
    "twelve forks ([answers]). Among them: dSafePassage gains the step gate (SA-11), the step's isolation contract, "
    "gov first for every step (SA-3), the hook unwiring, the retired-edited state and the stale lock moved from "
    "dShippedRelease (SA-2), a walk that recovers from a killed step, frozen landed steps, and windows counted from the "
    "first cut release (SA-8); act bindings are pushed for checks on any node (SA-10); `salted` is defined (SA-4); "
    "deploy.toml joins the minimal guard (SA-12); the finder is dTotalRecall's (SA-6) and the selector dFurnishedOrders' "
    "(SA-7); dConvergedCharter renders help/ from units (SA-5), retires /session-kickoff (SA-9) and walks the cycle by "
    "key; every set-valued key declares an empty-set rule; and nineteen bug classes record instances. "
    "(2) 17355b8b1 and a0b1a06c4 fold the owner's answers on the rest of the Skills: /build retires (SK-1), and the "
    "five question Skills stay as generated thin entries named gov-<name>, /gov-drift among them (SK-2). "
    "(3) 926106e87 records the adopter-instructions research, four returns and the design record " + B +
    "2026-10-19-build-PLAY-dClosedLoop-1-adopter-instructions.md, and 320c79646 folds the owner's answers IA-1 to IA-6: "
    "one guarded overlay, `.governance/instructions.toml`, tagged repo.; gov's units changed only by `amends` and "
    "`supersedes` edges pinned as <tag>@<hash>, or excluded by `instructions.exclude`; stale pins filed as orders by "
    "`instructions.stale`; a fixed set; a legacy block at install; and gov-only rules moved to gov's overlay by census. "
    "Review it as a design change. Does each fold land as the owner's answers and the [fold] plan say, the same way in "
    "every record it touches, and does any text still state what a fold replaced: /build or /session-kickoff as kept "
    "entries, /gov-drift-audit, the per-session card read after its retirement, `journal` renamed without its alias, "
    "`forked` for an edited retired file, the record finder or the bug-class selector on two builds, or deploy.toml as "
    "the home of adopter rules? Does every new clause sit on its own build or an ancestor, naming no later build's key "
    "or kind? Are the new catalogue keys consistent with the presets, the never-touch list and the owner's answers? "
    "Does each new gap state a fact its evidence supports, owned by the build whose unit closes it? Do dSafePassage's "
    "additions hold together within its ancestry? Is the adopter-instructions design consistent with the systems "
    "record's unit schema, the memory plan's edge grammar, P8, the step gate and the render gate? Does each bug-class "
    "instance describe its defect faithfully? A fold's own text is new surface: check it as hard as the text it "
    "replaced. This is run {run} of two independent runs on the same diff; read no other run's report. Write the "
    "report to {report}. Its head carries an H1, then, within its first twelve lines, the line `**Serves:** "
    "diff-review PLAY-dClosedLoop-1`. It carries exactly one `## Verdict:` line, whose token is CLEAN, CLEAN WITH FIXES "
    "or BLOCKED and nothing else.")
for run in ("A", "B"):
    report = R.format(run.lower())
    if pathlib.Path(report).exists():
        sys.exit(f"{report} exists")
    a = dict(base, scratch=(S / f"review-folds-{run.lower()}").as_posix(),
             context=CONTEXT.replace("{run}", run).replace("{report}", report))
    out = S / "adopt" / f"args-folds-{run.lower()}.json"
    out.write_text(json.dumps(a, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
    (S / "adopt" / f"args-folds-{run.lower()}.compact.json").write_text(json.dumps(a, ensure_ascii=False),
                                                                       encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
    print(f"run {run}: {a['kind']} {a['base'][:9]}..{a['head'][:9]}, {a['intensity']}, {len(a['specs'])} specs, "
          f"checklist {len(a['checklist'].splitlines())} lines, efforts {a['efforts']}, context "
          f"{len(a['context'].split())} words, report {report.rsplit('/', 1)[1]}")
````

### `gather_instruments.py`

Gathers research passes' shell commands, written files and web calls from their transcripts into one instruments record.

````python
"""Gather research passes' instruments from their transcripts: every shell command each researcher ran, every file it
wrote, and every web query and page it read, in order, as fenced text in one instruments record. The retrofit pass's
gatherer (`retrofit/gather_instruments.py`), widened to any number of runs and to the web calls a prior-art pass rests
on.

Usage: python -X utf8 gather_instruments.py <out-record-name> <title> <returns-line> <run>...   (from the worktree root)
  out-record-name  e.g. research-flow-instruments, saved as build/2026-10-19-build-PLAY-dClosedLoop-1-<name>.md
  title            the record's H1, after "Research instruments: "
  returns-line     one sentence naming the returns, written under the H1
  run              <tag>:<dispatch>:<question>:<transcript.jsonl>, one per research pass, in dispatch order

The transcript holds each call as the run sent it, whatever the shared scratch directory holds now. Fences are four
backticks, and a body holding a line that opens a fence is refused, to be filed by hand. Refuses to overwrite.

Edited after both runs, its output unchanged: the fence is built as FENCE, as the recorder's own is, because the
recorder refuses to embed a source holding the four-backtick string.
"""
import json
import pathlib
import sys

name, title, returns = sys.argv[1:4]
runs = [a.split(":", 3) for a in sys.argv[4:]]
OUT = pathlib.Path("memory/builds/dClosedLoop/build/2026-10-19-build-PLAY-dClosedLoop-1-%s.md" % name)
if OUT.exists():
    sys.exit("%s exists" % OUT)
KEEP = ("Bash", "Write", "WebSearch", "WebFetch")
FENCE = "`" * 4


def calls(src):
    for raw in pathlib.Path(src).read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        try:
            ev = json.loads(raw)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            continue
        msg = ev.get("message") if isinstance(ev, dict) else None
        if ev.get("type") != "assistant" or not isinstance(msg, dict):
            continue
        for c in msg.get("content", []):
            if isinstance(c, dict) and c.get("type") == "tool_use" and c.get("name") in KEEP:
                yield c["name"], c.get("input") or {}


parts = ["# Research instruments: %s\n" % title,
         "**Serves:** research PLAY-dClosedLoop-1\n",
         "Each pass's shell commands, written files, web queries and pages read, taken in order from its transcript, so "
         "nothing is retyped. The passes shared the session scratch directory, so a file there may hold another pass's "
         "content; these are what each pass sent. Reads of the tree (Read, Grep, Glob) are left out, as the retrofit "
         "pass's instruments left them out. %s\n" % returns]
total = {}
for tag, dispatch, question, src in runs:
    parts.append("## [%s] Dispatch %s: %s\n" % (tag, dispatch, question))
    k = 0
    for kind, inp in calls(src):
        k += 1
        if kind == "Write":
            body = inp.get("content", "")
            label = "Write `%s`" % pathlib.PurePosixPath(str(inp.get("file_path", "")).replace(chr(92), "/")).name
        elif kind == "WebSearch":
            body, label = inp.get("query", ""), "WebSearch"
        elif kind == "WebFetch":
            body, label = "%s\n%s" % (inp.get("url", ""), inp.get("prompt", "")), "WebFetch"
        else:
            body, label = inp.get("command", ""), "Bash"
        body = body.replace("\r\n", "\n").rstrip("\n")
        if any(ln.lstrip().startswith("```") for ln in body.split("\n")):
            sys.exit("%s call %d holds a fence line; file it by hand" % (tag, k))
        parts.append("%d. %s\n\n%stext\n%s\n%s\n" % (k, label, FENCE, body, FENCE))
    total[tag] = k
text = "\n".join(parts)
OUT.write_bytes(text.encode("utf-8"))
print("%s: %d bytes; calls %s" % (OUT, len(text.encode("utf-8")), total))
````

### `log_flow.py`

The session log's dispatch 122 to 126 rows, both runs' and the three researchers' agent lines, and three events.

````python
"""Record the paired closing review of the last three folds and the flow-and-roles adoption research in the session
log: dispatch rows 122 to 126 (run A 122, the three researchers 123 to 125, run B 126), every agent and returned line
as the roles kit derived them, and three events: the paired review, with run A's report set aside while run B ran; the
research pass; and the defect the today pass measured outside its question, flagged as a separate task.

Usage: python -X utf8 log_flow.py <agent-lines-runA.txt> <agent-lines-123-125.txt> <agent-lines-runB.txt>
       (from the worktree root)
"""
import pathlib
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, str(pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "expansions"))
from fold_lib import Record  # noqa: E402


def lines_of(path, n):
    got = [ln for ln in pathlib.Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8").replace("\r\n", "\n").split("\n")
           if ln.startswith(("- agent —", "- returned —"))]
    if len(got) != n:
        sys.exit(f"{path}: {n} agent and returned lines expected, read {len(got)}")
    return got


run_a, research, run_b = lines_of(sys.argv[1], 20), lines_of(sys.argv[2], 6), lines_of(sys.argv[3], 20)
F = "`" * 3
REC = "build/2026-10-19-build-PLAY-dClosedLoop-1-flow-roles-adoption.md"
L = Record("memory/builds/dClosedLoop/build/2026-10-14-build-PLAY-dClosedLoop-1-session-log.md")
row121 = [ln for ln in L.text.split("\n") if ln.startswith("| 121 |")]
if len(row121) != 1:
    sys.exit("no single dispatch row 121")
SHAPE = ("`tier2-review.js`, diff review, light: three `gov-diff-reviewer` lenses (correctness, seams, verification), "
         "five `gov-skeptic` batches and one `gov-synthesizer`, all at the owner's medium, run {} of two")
WHAT = ("The closing review of the last three folds, run twice at the owner's word: `320c79646` over `dd1ebb01b`, the "
        "shape audit's fold, the Skills' and the adopter instructions'")
ROWS = [
    (122, SHAPE.format("A"), WHAT, "the args, built by `build_args_folds.py`",
     "returned as `wf_32d759cc-d9a`, CLEAN WITH FIXES, 24 of 30 confirmed, 20 items, 1 high",
     "`reviews/2026-10-19-review-PLAY-dClosedLoop-1-folds-closing-a.md`"),
    (123, "gov-researcher, at the owner's medium effort",
     "The flow and roles adoption pass: how an adopter adds to or changes gov's flow and roles today, and what the next "
     "update does, measured on a scratch install",
     "`prompts/2026-10-19-prompt-PLAY-dClosedLoop-1-5-researcher.md`",
     "returned, 15m16s, 62.0k out: legs, run vocabularies and role files add beside gov's; tables typed into gov's code "
     "refuse an adopter role or workflow; an edited leg argv withholds the manifest, and a deleted gov leg returns "
     "unreported", "`build/2026-10-19-build-PLAY-dClosedLoop-1-research-flow-today.md`"),
    (124, "gov-researcher, at the owner's medium effort",
     "The pass: what the converged design decides about an adopter's own flow and roles, and what it leaves open",
     "`prompts/2026-10-19-prompt-PLAY-dClosedLoop-1-6-researcher.md`",
     "returned, 8m21s, 45.8k out: breakpoints, probe points, presets, playbooks, policy values and role prose decided; "
     "an item or role in a core step, and amending, replacing, disabling or surviving a change to a gov row, open; six "
     "contradictions", "`build/2026-10-19-build-PLAY-dClosedLoop-1-research-flow-design.md`"),
    (125, "gov-researcher, at the owner's medium effort",
     "The pass: prior art outside gov for adding and changing steps, checks and roles through upstream updates",
     "`prompts/2026-10-19-prompt-PLAY-dClosedLoop-1-7-researcher.md`",
     "returned, 7m57s, 39.2k out: eight families; an own namespace, pinned edges, a typed graph checked when composed "
     "and roles that declare their shapes; a meaning change under an unchanged type passes every mechanism",
     "`build/2026-10-19-build-PLAY-dClosedLoop-1-research-flow-prior-art.md`"),
    (126, SHAPE.format("B"), WHAT, "the args, built by `build_args_folds.py`",
     "returned as `wf_a3ab6ac1-aba`, CLEAN WITH FIXES, 21 of 23 confirmed, 17 items, 0 high",
     "`reviews/2026-10-19-review-PLAY-dClosedLoop-1-folds-closing-b.md`"),
]
new = "".join(f"| {n} | {who} | {what} | {brief} | 1799cb98 | {out} | {rec} |\n"
              for n, who, what, brief, out, rec in ROWS)
L.sub(row121[0] + "\n", row121[0] + "\n" + new, "dispatch rows")
L.insert_before("\n## Events\n",
                "\nThe last three folds' closing review, dispatches 122 and 126, derived from each run the same way:\n\n"
                + F + "text\n" + "\n".join(run_a + run_b) + "\n" + F + "\n"
                + "\nThe flow and roles adoption research, dispatches 123 to 125, derived from each run the same way:\n\n"
                + F + "text\n" + "\n".join(research) + "\n" + F + "\n", "agent lines")
L.insert_before("\n## Instruments\n", f"""
- 2026-10-19, session 1799cb98: the owner asked, "Run the reviews of the same shape (medium effort, twice) for the
  last three folds. While they're running, we'll review the next piece of the Flow and Role layers." Two light diff
  reviews of `320c79646` over `dd1ebb01b` ran one after the other, dispatches 122 and 126, their args differing only in
  the run label, the report path and the scratch path. Run A's report was moved out of the tree while run B ran, so run
  B could not read it, and restored byte for byte after (sha256 `af2916008b87`). The comparison is
  `build/2026-10-19-build-PLAY-dClosedLoop-1-folds-reviews-compared.md`.
- 2026-10-19, session 1799cb98: the owner chose "Adoption and customization (Recommended)" as the Flow and Role layers'
  next piece. Three researchers took one question each, dispatches 123 to 125, and `{REC}` answers the question,
  recommends a design and puts its forks to the owner. Each pass's commands and probes are in
  `build/2026-10-19-build-PLAY-dClosedLoop-1-research-flow-instruments.md`, and the adopter-instructions passes'
  (118 to 121), never gathered before, in `build/2026-10-19-build-PLAY-dClosedLoop-1-research-adopter-instruments.md`.
- 2026-10-19, session 1799cb98: the today pass measured a defect outside its question: in a default adopter install,
  `.claude/roles.json` names the review harnesses at `tools/workflows/`, where the kit is not installed, and the spawn
  guard refuses gov's own `tier2-review.js` (rc 2). This build writes no product code, so the fix was offered to the

""", "events")

### `clauses.py`

Prints a v2 chain row's clauses whole, the fold's reading aid.

````python
"""Print a v2 chain row's clauses whole, numbered, filtered by a regex: the fold's reading aid.

Usage: python -X utf8 clauses.py <build> [<regex>]   (from the worktree root)
Clauses split at '; ' outside parentheses, as the planned-unit count splits them.
"""
import re
import sys

V2 = "memory/builds/dClosedLoop/build/2026-10-14-build-PLAY-dClosedLoop-1-architecture-v2.md"
build, pat = sys.argv[1], (sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else ".")
rows = [ln for ln in open(V2, encoding="utf-8").read().split("\n") if ln.startswith(f"| {build} |")]
if len(rows) != 1:
    sys.exit(f"{len(rows)} rows for {build}")
cells = rows[0].split(" | ")
body = cells[3]
depth, cur, out = 0, "", []
i = 0
while i < len(body):
    ch = body[i]
    if ch == "(":
        depth += 1
    elif ch == ")":
        depth -= 1
    if depth == 0 and body.startswith("; ", i):
        out.append(cur)
        cur = ""
        i += 2
        continue
    cur += ch
    i += 1
out.append(cur)
for k, c in enumerate(out):
    if re.search(pat, c):
        print(f"[{k}] {c}\n")
print(f"{len(out)} clauses; gaps cell: {cells[4][:200]}")
````

````python
"""Fold the owner's answers to FA-1 to FA-7, the flow and roles adoption forks
(`build/2026-10-19-build-PLAY-dClosedLoop-1-flow-roles-adoption.md`), into v2, the systems record, the memory plan, the
gap register, the fates record and the design record itself, with the session log's event. FA-3 departed from the
recommendation: a repository may insert a stage of its own between two of gov's, and P20 is amended.

Usage: python -X utf8 fold_flow.py   (from the worktree root)
Every substitution matches exactly once or the script exits.
"""
import collections
import pathlib
import re
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, str(pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "expansions"))
from fold_lib import Record  # noqa: E402

B = "memory/builds/dClosedLoop/build/"
REC = "build/2026-10-19-build-PLAY-dClosedLoop-1-flow-roles-adoption.md"


def chain_row(rec, build):
    rows = [i for i, ln in enumerate(rec.text.split("\n")) if ln.startswith(f"| {build} |")]
    if len(rows) != 1:
        sys.exit(f"{len(rows)} chain rows for {build}")
    return rows[0]


def add_clauses(rec, build, clauses, gaps):
    lines = rec.text.split("\n")
    i = chain_row(rec, build)
    cells = lines[i].split(" | ")
    if len(cells) != 5:
        sys.exit(f"{build}: {len(cells)} cells")
    cells[3] = cells[3] + "".join("; " + c for c in clauses)
    if gaps:
        tail = cells[4]
        if not tail.endswith(" |"):
            sys.exit(f"{build}: the gaps cell does not end the row")
        cells[4] = tail[:-2] + ", " + ", ".join(gaps) + " |"
    lines[i] = " | ".join(cells)
    rec.text = "\n".join(lines)
    rec.done += 1

      "P8")

      "P20 (FA-3)")

      "gov's tagged kit releases, overlays, the install",

      "layers: overlays under distribution")
V.sub("and\n`tools/roles/house/policy.toml`'s `[effort]` and `[gates]`, their readers re-pointed in the fold's own unit (DA-H5).",
      "and\n`tools/roles/house/policy.toml`'s `[effort]`, into `roles.effort.*`, and `[gates]`, into each role definition's "
      "gate grant, their readers re-pointed in the fold's own unit (DA-H5, FA-6).", "policies: the house file's fold")
V.sub("| `instructions.exclude` | none, or a set of gov unit tags, a fixed unit and one another active unit requires "
      "refused | none | the adopter-instructions pass: the gov units a repository drops, as `charter.practices` does "

- **The systems record:** `workflow` is dBoundRoles' namespace and `lens` dCalibratedLens', the unit's row grammar

- **The memory plan:** the instruction overlay's pocket and the unit site take the flow and role rows.
- **The gap register:** `gap-flow-19`, `gap-roles-24` to `gap-roles-26`, `gap-test-21`, `gap-review-17`,

- **The fates record:** `house/policy.toml` folds as FA-6 says, and `workflows.toml`, `tier2-review.js` and the leg
  manifest take a repository's rows. `.unattended.conf`'s extension vocabularies gain a row of their own.

row goes. The design record's `[folded]` says so.

   `--for-diff` would have selected for each reviewed range (run it at those commits in a scratch clone), and compare
   with the classes of the findings confirmed: hits, misses, and noise (selected and never relevant). Count how many
   classes exist, how many ever matched a confirmed finding, and how often sessions call the lookup, from the session
   logs and records.
3. **Where a gotcha bites:** for a sample of confirmed findings with a class, the moment the mistake was made (an edit
   to which kind of file, which command, which operation), and whether any input available at that moment could have
   selected the class.
4. **Alternatives:** serving a class just in time when an agent is about to perform the risky operation (a PreToolUse
   hook matching the class's trigger), the orientation scout handing selected classes in the work order, the runtime
   injecting them per act, converting classes into gates and retiring the lookup, or retiring it outright. Include prior
   art: path-scoped rules (Cursor rules' globs, Copilot's `applyTo`, Claude Code's path-scoped rules), linters and
   Semgrep rules, and lessons-learned systems. Cite each outside source with its URL and date.

**Return**, in this order: the selection mechanics; the measured table of hits, misses and noise per review, with the
commands; the moment-of-mistake sample; the candidates, including retirement, each with the smallest test that would
make it LOSE and that test's result; and your pick.

""" + OUTSIDE
Q["q-p7-agent-cap.md"] = CONTEXT.format(n=7, quote=quote(pt[7])) + """
**Handed facts.** v2 bounds a workflow's agent cap by agent-cap's `FANOUT_CAP`; the register's `gap-rt-05` records that
fan-out is bounded per prompt, not in flight; Runtime's supervisor tracks acts and their sessions (dWellOiledMachine);
the shapes registry declares each workflow's fan and cap (dBoundRoles); and a review run's lenses fill five slots that
agent-cap counts. A session note on this node says agent-cap gives each prompt five direct `Agent` spawns, a slot frees
45 minutes after its claim, and task notifications have reset the budget: re-verify each claim, never act on it.

You are the one researcher on this point.

**Your question.** What does `tools/hooks/agent-cap.js` actually do, and what should replace it?
1. **Inventory:** every rule agent-cap enforces, with `path:line`, what each protects, and the configuration it reads
   (`.agent-cap.conf`, `FANOUT_CAP` and others).
2. **Measured behaviour:** on a copy under the temp root, pipe synthetic `PreToolUse` payloads through it and show the
   slot ledger's behaviour: per prompt or per window, the 45-minute expiry, what resets it, and what it never counts
   (agents in flight, Workflow agents, background agents). Quote the commands and outputs.
3. **Why per window:** whether a `PreToolUse` hook can know when an agent ends, and which hook events the harness
   offers that could count agents in flight (for example `SubagentStart` and `SubagentStop`), from the harness's
   documentation and this repository's own hook wiring.
4. **The design:** where an owner-adjustable limit on agents in flight belongs: its policy key and owning build, its
   enforcer (Runtime's supervisor, a hook pack, the harness's own settings), how it counts in flight reliably, and how
   each of agent-cap's other rules moves elsewhere on retirement, such as the Workflow script checks, harness admission,
   the spec-audit opt-in and the lens count.

**Return**, in this order: the rule inventory; the measured ledger behaviour with commands; the hook events available,
cited; candidates for the replacement, each with the smallest test that would make it LOSE and that test's result,
measured where possible; the relocation of each rule; and your pick.

""" + OUTSIDE
for name, text in Q.items():
    (N / name).write_text(text.rstrip("\n") + "\n", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
    print(name, len(text))
````

### `start_record.py`

Opens the night pass two's record with the owner's words, verbatim and whole.

````python
"""Open the night pass two's record: the owner's words, verbatim and whole, and how the pass runs. Later steps add the
research table, a section per point, the chain's impact, the parked forks and the closing review.

Usage: python -X utf8 start_record.py <night2-dir>   (from the worktree root); refuses to overwrite
"""
import pathlib
import sys

N = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1])
OUT = pathlib.Path("memory/builds/dClosedLoop/build/2026-10-19-build-PLAY-dClosedLoop-1-night-pass-two.md")
if OUT.exists():
    sys.exit(f"{OUT} exists")
words = (N / "owner-words-raw.txt").read_text(encoding="utf-8").rstrip("\n")
quoted = "\n".join("> " + ln if ln.strip() else ">" for ln in words.split("\n"))
text = f"""# The night pass two: the owner's seven points, worked unattended

**Serves:** research PLAY-dClosedLoop-1

While two review runs read the last three folds, the owner reviewed the Flow and Role layers' adoption piece, answered
its forks, and then handed over seven points to be worked unattended through the night. This record holds the words,
what the design held on each point, the research, the design worked in, and the forks parked for the owner's return.

## [words] The owner's words, 2026-10-19

{quoted}

## [method] How the pass runs

- **One point at a time.** Each point gets its own section: what the design already holds, what the research found,
  the design worked in, and its forks. Research runs ahead in waves, since a point's design waits on its returns.
- **Research.** Researchers run at the owner's medium effort, read-only, one question each. Each handoff is in
  `prompts/`, and each return is saved verbatim beside this record. Agent-cap admits five direct spawns at a time, so
  the questions go out in waves of at most five.
- **Forks.** Each fork's first option is the recommendation. The design as folded shows the recommendation, marked
  pending on its fork, as the first night pass did. The `NT` family numbers them.
- **Reviews.** The night's folds are reviewed twice, as two independent Tier-2 runs compared defect by defect, and
  the defects are folded before the report.
- **Bounds.** No product code, no merge and no push, as the build's brief says; the design map and the atlas are
  regenerated after each design change.
"""
OUT.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
print(OUT, len(text))
````

## [p1-scenarios] Point 1: scenarios, one method for flexible flows and workers

**What the design held** (dispatch 127). Six seams each carry part of a variant, and none of them selects one:
- the entry-point table, which picks only where a build starts;
- playbooks and `repeat`, a content recipe that enters at Design;
- presets, one per repository;
- the composition with its repository stages, one per repository (FA-1 to FA-7);
- the per-boundary policy sets, `review.breakpoints` and `probe.points`, repository-wide;
- the shape and lens registries.

Nothing records what kind of work a build is: none of the 173 build READMEs carries a kind, and the plan record has no
field for one. A structural change mid-build goes only through the overlay, and it moves every build at its next step
boundary. The shapes registry already expresses one agent (`single`), parallel agents (`per-unit`), mixed roles over
stages (`panel`), twin runs and experiments, with caps per workflow under agent-cap's fixed five, and a lens has been a
catalogue row since FA-1. The pass also found records disagreeing: the lens entering by an edit to the harness in
flow-steps and the review-system record, four shape kinds in the systems record against five, the closed kind set
without `item` or `lens`, the frame's transitions fixed though a splice may sit between stages, and the role matrix
silent on repository roles. Each is folded below.

**What outside systems teach** (dispatch 128). Eight families, none covering every case:
- configurable superset models (C-YAWL, GitLab `rules`), which only switch parts off;
- pinned templates included by reference (Azure `extends` with its required-template check, GitHub reusable
  workflows), safe but unrecorded mid-run;
- late-bound repertoires chosen per work item and refined by recorded rejections (YAWL worklets, Camunda ad-hoc
  subprocesses);
- case plans with discretionary items and sentries (CMMN);
- structure computed by code with versioned execution (Temporal, LangGraph): a probe ran a reordered variant to a
  run-time `KeyError` and compiled an orphan role without complaint;
- instance change with migration of compliant instances (ADEPT2, Camunda migration);
- model-chosen handoffs (the OpenAI Agents SDK, Claude's subagents), recorded only as transcripts;
- process mining, which sees a deviation only after the fact.

**The answer.** Today the flow bends in five places but has no unit for a variant, so none of the owner's cases has
one home. The recommendation gives it one: a build runs one composition, gov's rows, the repository's, the scenarios
it was placed under and its own recorded changes, pinned per step and checked whole.
1. **A scenario is a registered kind** (NT-1). A `scenario` row names the scenario it extends, an admission predicate
   over a request's facts, its entry, the rows of registered kinds it activates (stages, items, field patches,
   exclusions, roles, workflow entries, lens opt-ins, leg packs), a preset slot and caps. Gov ships some, a repository
   adds its own in its overlay, and every check runs on the composed result, so a scenario cannot reorder or drop a gov
   stage or touch the fixed set.
2. **Selection at placement** (NT-2). The orientation scout names the scenarios whose predicates hold over the request,
   with the facts; `placement.check` re-evaluates every predicate; the planner may re-pick at Plan; a later re-pick
   happens only at a step boundary. A request no scenario admits runs `flow.scenario-default`.
3. **Policy per scenario** (NT-3). A scenario's preset slot scopes a preset and overrides to its builds, never a key
   presets never touch, so a high-precision scenario can run strict while the repository runs standard.
4. **Changing a build's flow mid-build** (NT-4). A role proposes rows for its own build. Under `flow.adapt`'s default, a
   change that only adds items, roles, stages or stricter values applies unattended at the next step boundary and is
   recorded; one that removes, reorders or loosens waits for the owner while the build carries on. At each step
   boundary the build's witnessed path is compared with its pinned composition, so an unrecorded deviation files an
   order.
5. **Recording and promotion** (NT-5). Every change is kept in the build's folder. The Loop Review proposes a scenario
   from a change two or more builds carried, the owner ratifies it through `instructions.edit` with `promoted-from`
   edges to those changes, and builds in flight move to it only at a step boundary and only if they comply.
6. **The shipped set** (NT-6). Gov ships the scenarios its records already know: feature, amendment, patch,
   playbook-run and design-only, the last passing all five stages with record units, so P20 stands. Expansions
   register their own, and domain scenarios, a mobile application or a high-precision data system, are a repository's.
7. **Several scenarios and pipelines** (NT-7). A build may run several, unioned in a declared order. Two that set one
   field differently red at composition and wait for the owner, as `flow.scenario-conflict` says. A scenario may name
   the one that takes over at a step's exit, which makes an in-build pipeline, and a cross-build pipeline is builds
   filed with `depends-on`. Scenarios per feature or per unit wait on the owed feature and unit tables (`gap-flow-15`).
8. **Workflow shapes as data** (NT-8). A workflow entry declares its ordered stages, each with its role, fan, cap,
   effort and the rows it receives and returns, and the five kinds become named defaults over them. One agent, a
   parallel set, one step, several steps, mixed roles and variable caps are then all data, each cap at or under the
   repository's agent limit (point 7).
9. **Lenses** (NT-9). A lens is added as a catalogue row whose brief is a unit and removed by a swap or an exclusion;
   a repository lens records a replay result when one ran and never owes one.
10. **Cohesion.** One selector, the scenario, sits over one composition; one pin per step records what ran; one door,
    `instructions.edit`, writes every structural row; one check runs the whole. The six seams become fields of it.

**The owner's cases.**

| Case | Under the recommendation |
|---|---|
| An edge case needs its steps in another order and a new role inserted | a recorded change: `needs` patches reorder items, a repository role item is inserted, a repository stage may be spliced between gov's; gov's stages keep their order |
| A scenario per kind of work, picked by the runtime | `scenario` rows with admission predicates, chosen at placement and re-checked mechanically |
| Create or adapt a scenario on the fly, and record it | a build's recorded change, applied at a step boundary, kept in its folder, promoted by the Loop Review and the owner |
| Pick from a shipped set and build pipelines | gov's five, extended by the repository's; in-build successors at a step's exit, and cross-build `depends-on` |
| Reshape workflows | a workflow entry's ordered stages as data, the five kinds named defaults, caps under the agent limit |
| Add or remove a lens | a catalogue row, swapped or excluded |

**What it leaves for later.** Scenarios per feature or per unit wait on the feature and unit transition tables. Caps
above five wait on point 7. A change of meaning in prose (a lens brief reworded for one call) leaves no structural
deviation for the step-boundary comparison to see, the same limit the adoption pass found.

**Folded.** v2's P8, four `flow.*` keys with their preset rows, and clauses on dDeclaredLoop, dPlacedRequest,
dRankedPlan, dKeptSession, dBoundRoles and dCalibratedLens, each pending its fork; the foundations record's C3 gains
`item`, `lens` and `scenario`; flow-steps and the review-system record say a lens is data; the systems record has five
kinds, workflow stages as data and the `scenario` namespace; the adoption record's frame admits a splice; layer-roles'
matrix reads the composition; the memory plan's `promoted-from` takes a scenario source; and the register gains
`gap-flow-20`, `gap-flow-21` and `gap-review-18`.

## [forks] Parked for the owner, 2026-10-19

Each fork's first option is the recommendation, and the design as folded shows it, marked pending. Where the answer
sets a key's default, the options are the key's allowed values (P10); where it is a structural choice, it is a
decision.

| Fork | Question | Options, the recommendation first | What the answer sets |
|---|---|---|---|
| NT-1 | What is a scenario? | a registered kind: named, pinned overlay rows with a preset slot, chosen per build; presets and playbooks extended to carry structure; no scenarios, one composition per repository | a structural decision |
| NT-2 | Who picks a build's scenario? | the orientation scout at placement, `placement.check` re-evaluating its predicates, the planner able to re-pick at Plan; the owner, always; a table mapping request labels to scenarios | a structural decision, and `flow.scenario-default`'s value |
| NT-3 | May a scenario set policy for its builds? | yes, a preset and overrides scoped to its builds, never a key presets never touch; no, policy stays repository-wide | a structural decision |
| NT-4 | Who may change a build's own flow mid-build? | a role proposes, a change that only adds applies unattended at the next step boundary and is recorded, one that removes, reorders or loosens waits for the owner; the owner approves every change; no changes | `flow.adapt`'s default: additive-recorded, owner-approves, off |
| NT-5 | How does a recorded change become reusable? | the Loop Review proposes a scenario from a change two or more builds carried, and the owner ratifies it; only the owner promotes; never | `flow.promote`'s default: loop-proposes, owner-only, off |
| NT-6 | How does a design-only build end? | a `design-only` scenario passes all five stages with record units, P20 unchanged; P20 amended with a transition from Design to a terminal state | a structural decision |
| NT-7 | Can a build run several scenarios? | yes, unioned in a declared order, a conflict refused for the owner to order, with in-build successors at a step's exit; one scenario per build | `flow.scenario-conflict`'s default: refuse, declared-order |
| NT-8 | How are workflows reshaped? | each workflow entry's ordered stages as data, the five kinds named defaults; the five kinds only | a structural decision |
| NT-9 | How is a lens removed, and must a repository lens prove itself? | a swap or an exclusion, and a repository lens records a replay result when one ran but never owes one; swaps only; every repository lens owes the blind replay | a structural decision |
"""
R.done += 1
R.save()
print("folded point 1")
````

    lines = rec.text.split("\n")
